/LILIAN

Baltic Exchange Market Report 09 September 2026
Baltic Dry Index: 3620 (36)
Baltic Capesize Index: 6400 (87)
Baltic Panamax Index: 2414 (0)
Baltic Supramax Index: 1704 (11)
Baltic Handysize Index: 922 (9)
CAPESIZE
The market maintained its positive momentum today, with the BCI 182 5TC increasing by $788 to $58,041. In the Pacific, the C5 index pushed up a further 0.215 to $18.735, while the C3 index nudged 0.236 higher to $41.918. In the Pacific, sentiment remained slightly firmer, an operator's reported fixture at $19.05 for forward-loading dates overnight set a positive tone from the outset, with Owners opening offers in the low-to-mid $19s. While the pace of activity eased compared to previous sessions, Owners maintained a bullish stance. One miner was heard bidding around $18.30 before reportedly fixing at $18.50, while a second miner was said to have repeated yesterday's level of $18.40 on a Newcastlemax vessel. With two miners active alongside a healthy number of operator-controlled cargoes, underlying support remained evident despite the quieter trading environment. The Atlantic market remained supported, with sentiment positive despite minimal activity reported by brokers. There was talk of $42.00–$42.50 being paid on C3 for mid-October dates, although this remained unconfirmed. Bids were generally in the mid $41s against offers in the low to mid $42s.
PANAMAX
Market sources today reported a more active trading day in the Atlantic, with brokers highlighting an increase in fresh cargo supply on both the trans-Atlantic and fronthaul routes. However, the persistent surplus of open tonnage, especially off the North Continent continues to weigh on sentiment and cannot be overlooked. Sources have stated that Owners with tonnage open in the Atlantic are reportedly still favouring intra-basin employment, providing a degree of support to fronthaul rates. As a result, the volume of genuinely fixable tonnage is lower than tonnage lists initially suggest. In the Pacific, market participants have stated that a positive outlook remains as fundamentals support current levels especially with further talks of potential Cape stems being split. The North Pacific and Australia are said to be showing an increase in activity with the same reflected in the volume of reported fixtures today. The Ever Grace (82,039 2015) open Yeosu 13 September was said to have been placed on subjects with ETG for an Australian round trip, although a rate was not reported. The Star Diamond (93,406 2010) open Hong Kong 12 September and the Serifos (81,086 2015) open Kashima 13/14 September were both reported as fixed. The Ocean Changhong (88,083 2008) open Hadong was said to have fixed a Pacific round at $23,000, but no other information was heard. The P5TC edged up by $1 to finish at $21,725.
SUPRAMAX
As we pass the mid week point of the week, there seemed to be few reported trades again, regardless of the passing of the Labor Day disruption. Despite the lack of information, the Index again showed positive returns with the 11TC average up $134 to close at $21,537. The North American market again returned the biggest gains with the fronthaul now outpacing the trans Atlantic market, whilst the Continent appeared quiet apart from some additional Russian stems. The East Mediterranean fronthaul market was marked up again in thin volume and the West Mediterranean saw more backhaul and gypsum stems, which helped the South Atlantic market as it might reduce the ballasters on the nearby positions. In the East the market remained steady in the North, whilst the South was saw rates increasing for trips to India/Bangladesh, but the shorter trips back to China appeared to soften slightly as Owners had to discount to stay in the area.
HANDYSIZE
Building on yesterday’s momentum, the Atlantic market continued to show a steady upward trend. The BHSI closed the day at 922, while the 7TC average rose by $178 to settle at $16,603. In the Continent and Mediterranean, fundamentals remained firm, although reported activity was limited. The South Atlantic and US Gulf maintained their strength, particularly in the US Gulf, where tight tonnage for end September and steady demand pushed rates well above previous levels. The Pacific market also maintained a firm tone, with numbers holding steady and some routes showing modest improvement. The HPC Pioneer (38,215 2011) open Jakarta 9–10 September was fixed from Dampier to China with salt at $19,000 by Berge, while a 33,000-dwt vessel open South Korea was reported fixed for a trip to Southeast Asia at $16,000, although further details were not disclosed.

Market Fundamentals
Chinese Generators Curb Coal Buying

China's largest state-owned generators are pulling back on coal purchases, with no fresh import tender requirements seen since 7 September, as rising coal prices and strong renewable generation push coal-fired power plants further into losses, McCloskey reports. China Electricity Council (CEC) data show coal burn fell 12.6% year-on-year in the week to 3 September, while total plant inventories stood at 103.83 Mt (-0.3 Mt week-on-week), covering 19.8 days of consumption. Seaborne coal stocks rose to 29.1 Mt (+0.2 Mt), while burn at those plants fell 13.6% year-on-year.

Trading Commentary
Cape
Cape FFA’s traded with a softer tone today. September opened around 54,500–54,750 before easing to 53,900 through late morning and falling to 53,000 during the afternoon. October moved from 51,000–51,400 early to around 50,250–50,500 by late morning, before weakening further to 49,500–49,800 in the afternoon. The Oct v Nov spread widened and strengthened early on up to 4050, before being sold back down to 3500 as the front-end support eased. November fell from 47,350 early to 46,750 around midday and 46,000 later on. December eased from 44,500–44,600 to 43,900. Q4 traded around 47,750–47,900 early before falling to 46,500–46,750 later. Q1 27 moved from around 32,500 to 31,700–32,000. The Q4 v Q1 roll narrowed and weakened down to a low of 14750. Overall, the curve weakened through the session, with the main activity concentrated across the front end.

PMX
PMX felt less supported today. September was relatively steady around 22,200–22,300 for most of the session. October traded mainly around 24,000–24,100, briefly reaching 24,250 early and 24,200 in the afternoon. November opened around 23,450–23,500 before easing to 23,250 later on, while December traded around 22,250.
